policy_findings.title: Passwordless Dangerous Sudo Binary allowed: systemctl (command)
policy_findings.description:
The user(s) [deploy] can run '/usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx.service' via sudo as [root] without a password (NOPASSWD) with the 'command' capability (inherited via less). This can enable privilege escalation if the inherited 'less' behavior can be triggered.
GTFObins Context: Inherits command behavior from less.
Note: Pager escape requires a TTY with paged output and is typically restricted on systemd >= 247 (LESSSECURE=1 under sudo) unless PAGER/SYSTEMD_PAGER/LESSSECURE is preserved or overridden.
Note: Environment-variable techniques (e.g. LESSOPEN/VISUAL/EDITOR) require SETENV or matching env_keep permissions.
policy_findings.remediation: Remove this binary from sudoers or replace it with a tightly scoped wrapper script.
policy_findings.remediation_code:
# Replace direct 'systemctl' (command) access with a root-owned wrapper script (EXEC: required when global Defaults noexec is active):
deploy ALL = (root) PASSWD: EXEC: sha256:<digest> /usr/local/sbin/safe-systemctl-wrapper.sh ""
policy_findings.exploit_poc:
# Via less (trigger with systemctl):
systemctl
# From less:
LESSOPEN='/path/to/command # %s' less /etc/hosts

policy_findings.title: Direct Text Editor Execution via Sudo
policy_findings.description: The command '/usr/bin/vim /etc/nginx/nginx.conf' allowed for user(s) [deploy] invokes a text editor directly under sudo. Text editors typically allow escaping to a shell or editing arbitrary system files. Use 'sudoedit' instead to safely edit files with current user privileges.
policy_findings.remediation: Replace direct text editor execution rules with 'sudoedit' permissions for specific files.
